source: Actual preview Cookie sessions for two real GitHub accounts in isolated ephemeral Chromium contexts
deploymentMetadataProvenance: Source commits and immutable Worker versions supplied by the release owner; this evidence review made no remote requests.

manifest.fixtures: Only new QA invitation/membership, shared expense, key and optional category

uiEvidence: Owner created one Viewer invitation; the second account accepted it and the UI selected the shared ledger.
Owner used manual Reload and waited for the current members response before saving Editor and Admin roles.
Editor created and edited one new QA Shared pool expense through the normal expense form; POST 201 and PATCH 200 were confirmed.
Owner removed the new membership through the Members confirmation UI; DELETE 204 was confirmed.
restEvidence: Each account authenticated as its expected stable GitHub user ID and retained its own personal workspace; Owner Free/Pro prerequisite avoided automatic model calls.
One recipient-owned workspace-revision key was created through REST, worked before the role change, and returned 403 after Editor changed to Admin. Key assertions omitted Cookie credentials.
Current Admin profile reported manageProjects permission and GET of the existing archived QA project returned 200; no new project was created.
After removal, the shared-workspace Cookie request returned 404 and the old key was denied with an allowed 403/404; the recipient personal workspace remained accessible with 200.
Cleanup read the current QA expense before soft deletion, revoked the newly created key, confirmed the invitation was no longer pending, and archived the newly created QA category.
counterUnits: HTTP requests and mutation responses; these counts are not D1 rows read/written.
membershipCleanup: The newly joined membership was already removed by the main UI action and its access denial was verified before cleanup.
limitations: Projects create, multi-repository/Organization filter, detail, search, Reports/CSV, archive/reactivate and Viewer read-only controls plus actual 403 are evidenced by the original baseline checks. Its original cached-members runner failure remains false and unchanged.

Admin project access, team-key creation/invalidation and post-removal permission assertions used REST; invitation acceptance, role changes, Shared pool expense create/edit and membership removal used the UI.
The follow-up read the existing archived QA project and created no additional project. Soft-deleted expenses and archived QA categories retain ordinary accounting history.
No real payment, live subscription change, model request, direct remote SQL, screenshot, trace, storageState or credential file was used.
